back: The degree to which inherent characteristics of a deliverable or process help meet or exceed the project's objectives.
Conformance to acceptance criteria, the definition of done, fitness for use and overall efficiency.
Performance, conformity, reliability, resilience, satisfaction, uniformity, efficiency, sustainability, compliance.
Using project processes effectively and following standards; related to regulations, compliance and audits.
Deliverables that meet defined specifications; related to product design, testing and defects.

front: Where quality sits in the 40 processes
back: Plan Scope Management (quality plan, test and inspection planning); Manage Quality Assurance; Monitor and Control Scope; Validate Scope.
An attribute a deliverable must have to meet or exceed a target objective.
Attributes and how compliance is checked: on-time tasks, CPI, failure rates, defects per day, downtime, satisfaction, test coverage.
Standards, objectives, roles, deliverables and processes reviewed, planned quality activities, tools, nonconformance and improvement procedures.
Audits, checklists, affinity and cause-and-effect diagrams, flowcharts, decision-making, problem-solving, process improvement.
Quality reports, change requests, plan and document updates.
Usually by people outside the project; finds good practices and nonconformities, shares practices, helps improve, adds lessons learned.
Quality issues, recommended corrective actions and a summary of quality control findings.
Verified: passed quality control (Monitor and Control Scope). Accepted: formally accepted in Validate Scope.
Shows whether a process is stable. Control limits are statistical; specification limits come from the requirements.
Fishbone or Ishikawa: traces an effect back to its root cause, branch by branch.
Comparing products, processes and practices with comparable organizations, for ideas and a basis for measurement.
Prevention (training, documented processes, equipment, time) and appraisal (testing, inspections, audits).
Internal failure (rework, scrap) and external failure (liabilities, warranty work, complaints, lost business).
The balance where more prevention and appraisal is no longer cost-effective; testing quality in late usually fails.
Less rework avoids wasted natural resources and emissions; sustainability is also a quality dimension.
Plan-do-check-act (PDCA), Lean, Total Quality Management, Six Sigma, Five Focusing Steps.
Finds the basic reason for a variance, defect or risk; when all root causes are removed, the problem does not recur.
Definition of done, continuous integration, testing at all levels (automated), ATDD, TDD, BDD, spikes.
Predictive: usually formal. Agile: formal or informal, depending on the context.
